question: Does giving the model a protected or demographic attribute improve detection enough to justify using it?

sensitive_columns.meaning: customer age as of alert date

design.family: xgboost at default configuration (no tuning inside an arm)
design.feature_ranking: the fold's own outer-train ranking, computed once and shared by every arm; no arm re-ranks
design.forcing_rule: a forced column is ADDED to the top 120 rather than swapped for the 120th, so a null result is not confounded by the loss of a wanted feature

gender_handling.why_injection: F3892 is removed by the firewall before the frame exists, so it cannot be ranked. Rebuilding the ranking with it admitted would change every column's rank and stop the arms being paired on identical pools; injecting the single column holds everything else fixed.
gender_handling.not_answered_by_this_run: whether stability selection would have CHOSEN gender if offered. This run answers whether a model that has it beats one that does not, which is the question the policy turns on.

F3890.note: null means the selector gave it zero importance in every inner fold, so it never entered the ranking

F3891.note: null means the selector gave it zero importance in every inner fold, so it never entered the ranking

F3894.note: null means the selector gave it zero importance in every inner fold, so it never entered the ranking

baseline.what: the shipped pool: the fold's own top 120, untouched

sensitive_excluded.what: geography, occupation and age struck from the fold ranking before the top 120 is taken - a no-op in any fold that did not rank one of them inside 120, which is the finding

gender_forced.what: top 120 plus F3892 GENDER, re-admitted through the frame builder's fairness-ablation switch

sensitive_forced.what: top 120 plus all three admissible demographics

all_four_forced.what: top 120 plus every column Description.xlsx marks sensitive

sensitive_excluded.yardstick: paired on identical outer folds - judge against std_of_paired_diff=0.00044, NOT against the project's 0.0905 unpaired seed-noise floor

geography_forced.yardstick: paired on identical outer folds - judge against std_of_paired_diff=0.01319, NOT against the project's 0.0905 unpaired seed-noise floor

occupation_forced.yardstick: paired on identical outer folds - judge against std_of_paired_diff=0.01141, NOT against the project's 0.0905 unpaired seed-noise floor

age_forced.yardstick: paired on identical outer folds - judge against std_of_paired_diff=0.01392, NOT against the project's 0.0905 unpaired seed-noise floor

gender_forced.yardstick: paired on identical outer folds - judge against std_of_paired_diff=0.01158, NOT against the project's 0.0905 unpaired seed-noise floor

sensitive_forced.yardstick: paired on identical outer folds - judge against std_of_paired_diff=0.01136, NOT against the project's 0.0905 unpaired seed-noise floor

all_four_forced.yardstick: paired on identical outer folds - judge against std_of_paired_diff=0.01391, NOT against the project's 0.0905 unpaired seed-noise floor

decision_rule.text: a sensitive attribute is re-admitted to the accepted primary model only if its arm's mean paired difference is positive AND the sign test rejects at 0.05. Fixed before the run. Anything else - including a positive mean that the sign test cannot separate from noise - is KEEP_EXCLUSION.
decision_rule.note: sensitive_excluded is scored and reported but is not a candidate for re-admission; it is the control that shows what removing the attributes costs.

slice_audit.score: mean of the 3 outer-fold OOF score matrices, which is how the companion audit ranks dev rows
slice_audit.group_source: raw columns, not model features - so gender can be sliced on even though the model never sees it

reporting_rule.selection_rate: reported only when the group has >= 50 rows
reporting_rule.recall: reported only when the group has >= 3 positives, matching docs/FAIRNESS_AND_SENSITIVE_FEATURE_AUDIT.md so the two documents can be read together

slice_audit.impossible_age_note: ages below zero exist in this extract and fall in the '< 25' bin; counted here so the bin does not hide them

interpretation: the sensitive_excluded arm is the control that matters most: if it is identical to baseline on every fold, then the exclusion policy costs nothing because the selector never wanted the attributes in the first place, and no amount of paired statistics is needed to say so
